items.title: 14.10.1 Main health risks associated with air pollution

items: Respiratory diseases: ozone, particulate matter and nitrogen dioxide increase asthma symptoms and trigger asthma attacks; long-term exposure may lead to chronic cough and respiratory infections such as pneumonia.
Cardiovascular diseases: particulate matter and other pollutants raise the risk of heart attack by causing inflammation, blood-vessel damage, high blood pressure and finally stroke.
Cancer: prolonged exposure to certain pollutants, especially particulate matter and carcinogenic compounds such as benzene, causes lung cancer.
Reproductive and developmental effects: air pollution may harm reproductive health and fertility in men and women, and premature birth and developmental problems in children may occur.

blocks.prompt: Evaluate the potential health risks of air pollution for a family living beside a busy road.
blocks.explanation: Daily traffic pollution exposes them to PM, NO2, CO, ozone and benzene: the children risk asthma and stunted lung development, the adults chronic bronchitis, raised blood pressure, heart attack and stroke, and all of them a higher lifetime risk of lung cancer; a pregnant mother risks premature birth. The risk grows with the years of exposure.

items: Risks: respiratory (asthma, pneumonia), cardiovascular (heart attack, stroke), cancer (PM, benzene), reproductive and developmental (fertility, premature birth).
